[PATH:empirical] Longitudinal benchmark study comparing explicit causal graph models (e.g., CausalGAN, DO-Transformers) against standard deep RL on the 'Minecraft-like' open-ended task suite (e.g., NetHack, Crafter) for 20-year projection via scaling laws — Directly tests whether explicit causal modules improve meta-learning and goal formation in non-stationary environments; if performance plateaus far below human-level, it refutes the hypothesis; if scaling trends suggest convergence, it confirms insufficiency.

[PATH:theoretical] Theoretical analysis of expressive capacity: prove or disprove that any polynomial-time causal-graph-augmented deep architecture can implement arbitrary open-ended goal-formation algorithms (e.g., Bayesian program synthesis or universal planning) without exponential sample complexity — Establishes fundamental computational limits; if provably insufficient for the scope, the hypothesis is confirmed; if a constructive proof exists, it is refuted.

[PATH:literature] Systematic literature review of all published attempts (2015–2025) to use causal graph modules for long-horizon, cross-domain transfer in robotics and game AI, focusing on failure modes like catastrophic forgetting and goal drift — Aggregates empirical evidence on whether such architectures have ever demonstrated human-level adaptability; a lack of positive results supports the hypothesis, while any counterexample refutes it.

scope.domain: any task requiring open-ended goal formation and meta-learning across diverse, non-stationary environments

[PATH:empirical] Longitudinal benchmark study comparing causal-graph-augmented deep learning systems (e.g., causal GANs, NCMs) against human performance on open-ended reasoning tasks (e.g., ARC, Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus) with annual evaluations over 10 years — Directly tests whether causal augmentation closes the gap to human-level general reasoning; systematic tracking of progress or stagnation would confirm or refute insufficiency by 2044.

[PATH:theoretical] Theoretical analysis of computational complexity and sample efficiency of causal discovery and inference in high-dimensional, non-stationary environments (e.g., proving that exact causal structure learning from limited data is NP-hard or requires super-polynomial resources) — If causal modules cannot scale to the complexity of real-world open-ended tasks without exponential resource demands, this provides a fundamental limitation supporting the hypothesis.

[PATH:literature] Literature review of current limitations and failure modes in causal deep learning systems (e.g., Pearl's 'causal hierarchy' challenges, inability to handle unknown confounders, lack of transfer across causal contexts) from top AI conferences (NeurIPS, ICML, UAI) over the past 5 years — Synthesizing documented bottlenecks (e.g., poor out-of-distribution generalization, fragility to spurious correlations) can indicate whether causal augmentation alone is insufficient for AGI-level adaptability.

[PATH:empirical] Perform a controlled empirical comparison of current causal-graph-augmented deep learning systems (e.g., NEMO, CausalGAN, or Do-calculus-based architectures) against a self-supervised world model trained on raw sensory data (e.g., video prediction with contrastive learning) on a suite of out-of-distribution reasoning tasks (e.g., the Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus or the CausalWorld benchmark). — This directly tests whether explicit causal graph modules alone are sufficient for human-level generalization or whether a self-supervised world model is necessary. If the causal-graph systems match or exceed the world model on transfer and reasoning, the hypothesis is weakened; if they fail, the hypothesis gains support.

[PATH:literature] Survey and synthesize recent literature on self-supervised learning approaches that implicitly learn causal structure from raw data (e.g., models based on time-contrastive learning, latent causal discovery, or object-centric representations) and compare their performance on common-sense reasoning benchmarks to those using human-engineered causal graphs. — This provides a broad evidence base to assess whether the field is converging on the necessity of self-supervised causal learning. A trend showing that such models match or surpass hand-crafted graph approaches would support the hypothesis; a lack of such trend would refute it.

[PATH:theoretical] Develop a theoretical analysis characterizing the computational and sample complexity of learning causal structures from raw sensory data vs. using pre-specified causal graphs, focusing on the limits of each approach for achieving human-level generalization and transfer in open-ended domains. — This can clarify whether there are fundamental information-theoretic or algorithmic barriers that make explicit graph modules insufficient without self-supervised learning. If theory shows that raw-sensory causal learning is necessary for certain types of reasoning, the hypothesis is confirmed; if not, it is refuted.
